meta.waveRule: Wave 1 = broken codegen (the generated product fails to build or crashes on first use) plus self-contained wire/migration fixes — file-disjoint, fully parallel, except M-T6.48 which conflictsWith M-T6.46 on java/emit/wire.ts and must stack or sequence. Wave 2 = decision-gated or merge-gated (M-T6.47 after #2631 merges; M-T5.22 carries the owner ruling; M-T9.37 after M-T6.46 or with a ratcheted java waiver). Wave 3 = structural (the codec seam after the concrete fixes inform it; the runtime legs after the fixes they would flag).
meta.processRule: Every task follows the repo rules: re-sync onto fresh main first, verify the finding is still live (this register rots like any other), open a DRAFT PR naming the mission ID and files before implementing, mutation-prove any gate the task adds (revert via file copy, never git checkout), delete any waiver the fix closes in the SAME PR, and fix ships WITH its witness — the fixture/probe named in the task, not a promise of one. Decisions embedded in mission texts are proposed defaults: overridable in draft-PR review, not silently.

Then add the corpus witness (a derived 0.1+0.2 field) and bring the exact-side backends into rule compliance. Also carries: the node decimal.js 20-digit precision question, the inbound precision-acceptance skew (java unlimited vs dotnet 28-29 vs double-clamped), and the numeric doc-drift fixes (language.md host table, collection-ops sum signature -> docs:stdlib regen).
